statements.status_notes: The compatibility images ship Nmap and its NSE scripts. A zero-length TCP option can cause unbounded allocation in nselib/packet.lua. The upstream fix is commit 7ef4ee030a0023fe22616387a000032e1a678b6a, included in Nmap 7.991; a compatible packaged fix and its validation remain under investigation. See https://github.com/nmap/nmap/commit/7ef4ee030a0023fe22616387a000032e1a678b6a and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-72712

The compatibility images ship Nmap 7.95. Crafted truncated IPv6 extension headers can cause out-of-bounds reads and a scanner crash during raw IPv6 scans. The upstream fix is commit bb6754e76bb1686315008e1aa1c40202a513fb83; a compatible packaged fix and its validation remain under investigation. See https://github.com/nmap/nmap/commit/bb6754e76bb1686315008e1aa1c40202a513fb83 and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-58058

The compatibility images ship the Nmap scanner, including service-version detection. A crafted TCP service response can exhaust the scanner stack during -sV scans. Debian tracks this as an unfixed issue with unimportant urgency; applicability and remediation remain under investigation. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2018-15173

Only ncat ships from the nmap source package (/usr/bin/ncat); the nmap port-scanner binary that CVE-2018-15173 affects is not installed in this image.
